Try a different weighting method – softmax_neg_error – to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over inverse_error.
test a simple robust aggregation (median) to see if it beats weighted given strong trend/seasonality.
Testing a simple mean aggregation to see if averaging all models beats the median and weighted combos, given strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability; a DBA (dynamic Bayesian averaging) might capture shifting model strengths.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models.
test a per‑horizon weighted combination (best_per_horizon) to see if varying weights by horizon improves over global weighted.
test a weighted combination on the reduced, highly ranked pool (pool4) using inverse_error weights to see if focusing on the top models improves over global weighted.
Test a per‑model weighted combo on a smaller, more diverse pool (pool4) using softmax_neg_error to see if a tighter pool with aggressive weighting improves over the current leader median.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but moderate ranking stability; a trimmed mean over a reduced pool may reduce noise from correlated models.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.918. Series context: trend strength 0.9991 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.384); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.032.
